content.thinking: The package reads `ARGS` from `/etc/default/prometheus-node-exporter`, so I'll write the role with a guard against non-loopback binds and set the llama workers' default host to `127.0.0.1`, fixing the actual exposure cause.

input.command:
cd ~/Projects/aihost && mkdir -p roles/node_exporter/{defaults,tasks,handlers,templates,meta} && cat > roles/node_exporter/meta/main.yml <<'EOF'
---
galaxy_info:
  author: aihost
  description: Host metrics exporter (CPU, memory, disk, network, systemd units) plus the textfile collector for aihost GPU metrics.
  license: MIT
dependencies: []
EOF
cat > roles/node_exporter/defaults/main.yml <<'EOF'
---
# Host metrics for a future Prometheus. CPU saturation matters most on this host: decode is bound by a
# single CPU thread, so per-core usage is the evidence that explains inference speed.
node_exporter_enabled: false
node_exporter_package: prometheus-node-exporter
# Loopback until a Prometheus host exists; widening it is a deliberate, explicit decision.
node_exporter_listen_address: "127.0.0.1:9100"
node_exporter_allow_non_loopback: false
# Files written atomically by the monitoring role (aihost-metrics.timer): GPU thermals, energy, GT activity.
node_exporter_textfile_dir: /var/lib/local-ai/metrics
# Unit-state series are limited to the inference stack (the pattern is anchored by node_exporter itself).
# No backslashes, dollar signs or spaces: the value travels through systemd's EnvironmentFile unchanged.
node_exporter_systemd_unit_include: "aihost-.*[.]service|llama-.*[.]service|vllm-top-console[.]service"
EOF
cat > roles/node_exporter/templates/prometheus-node-exporter.default.j2 <<'EOF'
# Managed by Ansible (role node_exporter). Read by the packaged systemd unit as $ARGS.
ARGS="--web.listen-address={{ node_exporter_listen_address }} --collector.textfile.directory={{ node_exporter_textfile_dir }} --collector.systemd --collector.systemd.unit-include={{ node_exporter_systemd_unit_include }}"
EOF
cat > roles/node_exporter/handlers/main.yml <<'EOF'
---
- name: Restart node exporter
  ansible.builtin.systemd_service:
    name: prometheus-node-exporter.service
    state: restarted
  when: not ansible_check_mode
EOF
cat > roles/node_exporter/tasks/main.yml <<'EOF'
---
- name: Refuse a non-loopback listen address unless it was explicitly allowed
  ansible.builtin.assert:
    that:
      - node_exporter_listen_address is match('^(127[.]0[.]0[.]1|localhost|\[::1\]):[0-9]+$') or (node_exporter_allow_non_loopback | bool)
      - node_exporter_systemd_unit_include is not search('[\\$ ]')
    fail_msg: >-
      node_exporter_listen_address must be loopback (set node_exporter_allow_non_loopback=true to publish it
      deliberately), and the systemd unit pattern must not contain backslashes, dollar signs or spaces.
  when: node_exporter_enabled | bool

- name: Install node exporter from the distribution archive
  ansible.builtin.apt:
    name: "{{ node_exporter_package }}"
    state: present
  when: node_exporter_enabled | bool

- name: Ensure the textfile collector directory exists
  ansible.builtin.file:
    path: "{{ node_exporter_textfile_dir }}"
    state: directory
    owner: root
    group: root
    mode: "0755"
  when: node_exporter_enabled | bool

- name: Configure node exporter arguments
  ansible.builtin.template:
    src: prometheus-node-exporter.default.j2
    dest: /etc/default/prometheus-node-exporter
    owner: root
    group: root
    mode: "0644"
  when: node_exporter_enabled | bool
  notify: Restart node exporter

- name: Enable and start node exporter
  ansible.builtin.systemd_service:
    name: prometheus-node-exporter.service
    enabled: true
    state: started
  when:
    - node_exporter_enabled | bool
    - not ansible_check_mode
EOF

"""Contract for the node_exporter role and the loopback-only worker binding (no host needed)."""
from __future__ import annotations

import re
from pathlib import Path

import jinja2
import yaml

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
ROLE = ROOT / "roles" / "node_exporter"


def _defaults() -> dict:
    return yaml.safe_load((ROLE / "defaults/main.yml").read_text())


def _render() -> str:
    return jinja2.Template((ROLE / "templates/prometheus-node-exporter.default.j2").read_text()).render(**_defaults())


def test_defaults_publish_nothing_beyond_loopback_and_are_off_until_enabled():
    d = _defaults()
    assert d["node_exporter_enabled"] is False
    assert d["node_exporter_listen_address"].startswith("127.0.0.1:")
    assert d["node_exporter_allow_non_loopback"] is False


def test_arguments_wire_the_textfile_collector_and_a_safe_systemd_filter():
    args = re.search(r'^ARGS="(.*)"$', _render(), re.M).group(1)
    d = _defaults()
    assert f"--web.listen-address={d['node_exporter_listen_address']}" in args
    assert f"--collector.textfile.directory={d['node_exporter_textfile_dir']}" in args
    assert "--collector.systemd" in args
    pattern = re.search(r"--collector.systemd.unit-include=(\S+)", args).group(1)
    assert not re.search(r"[\\$ ]", pattern), "the value travels through systemd's EnvironmentFile unchanged"
    assert re.fullmatch(pattern, "aihost-llama-worker1.service") and re.fullmatch(pattern, "vllm-top-console.service")
    assert not re.fullmatch(pattern, "ssh.service")


def test_the_guard_accepts_loopback_and_rejects_anything_else_unless_allowed():
    tasks = yaml.safe_load((ROLE / "tasks/main.yml").read_text())
    guard = next(t for t in tasks if "assert" in t["ansible.builtin.assert"] or True)["ansible.builtin.assert"]["that"][0]
    pattern = re.search(r"match\('(.+?)'\)", guard).group(1)
    for ok in ("127.0.0.1:9100", "localhost:9100", "[::1]:9100"):
        assert re.match(pattern, ok), ok
    for bad in ("0.0.0.0:9100", "10.0.8.5:9100", ":9100", "9100", "127.0.0.1.evil.com:9100"):
        assert not re.match(pattern, bad), bad
    assert "node_exporter_allow_non_loopback" in guard


def test_the_scoped_playbook_includes_the_role_only_when_enabled():
    play = yaml.safe_load((ROOT / "playbooks/inference.yml").read_text())[0]
    entry = next(r for r in play["roles"] if r.get("role") == "node_exporter")
    assert "node_exporter_enabled" in entry["when"]


def test_llama_workers_listen_on_loopback_by_default():
    defaults = yaml.safe_load((ROOT / "roles/llama_cpp_container/defaults/main.yml").read_text())
    assert defaults["llama_cpp_container_host"] == "127.0.0.1"
EOF

content.text:
Items 1, 2 and 4 are applied through the playbook, with 0 failures, and verified live. aihost is committed on `main`, 12 commits ahead of origin, and nothing is pushed.

**1. node_exporter (new role)**
- Installed from the Ubuntu archive (1.10.2) and bound to `127.0.0.1:9100` only. The role refuses a non-loopback address unless you explicitly allow it.
- It's serving about 2,000 metric lines: per-core CPU, memory, disk and network, plus the systemd state of the gateway, workers and console.
- It reads the textfile collector with `node_textfile_scrape_error 0`, so the `aihost_gpu_*` series are present.

**2. Thermal limits**
- I changed the plan here, and the evidence is why. Your role says alerts must fire below the 90 °C benchmark guardrail, so a per-sensor limit that loosened thresholds would break that design. The kernel limits are pkg 100 °C and vram 105 °C, and loads have peaked in the 60s–70s, so my earlier "false pages from VRAM" premise has no data behind it.
- A sensor's alert thresholds are now `min(configured, kernel limit − margin)`, so a kernel limit can only tighten alerting. The margins are 25 and 15, which reproduce today's 75/85 for the 100 °C sensors.
- The exporter now publishes each sensor's kernel limit (`aihost_gpu_temperature_limit_celsius`, 40 series) so dashboards can show headroom.
- The alert log now names the sensor that triggered the alert.
- On this hardware the thresholds didn't change.

**4. Workers**
- The cause was `llama_cpp_container_host: 0.0.0.0`. The ufw rules only masked port 8000, with a leftover "temporary B0" deny, while 8001 was open to all of `10.0.0.0/8`.
- Both workers now listen on `127.0.0.1`. From the LAN, ports 8000, 8001 and 9100 all fail to connect. The gateway reports both workers healthy, and both aliases route and answer 200.
- Nothing needed the workers from the LAN: OpenCode, Nexus, the gateway, vllm-top and the benchmark all use the gateway or localhost.

**Tests:** 185 related tests pass in the targeted run: 5 for the node_exporter role, plus 9 new thermal and exporter tests. The live `gpu.prom` still passes the strict exposition validator (12 families, 103 series).

I did not touch the host firewall. The two stale "AIHost-B0-temporary" deny rules in ufw are now redundant, but ufw is OS-level and removing rules risks a lockout. I'd clean them up deliberately, so say if you want that.

Next on my list from earlier are:
- dashboards and alert rules as code;
- streaming from the workers through the gateway;
- standing up Prometheus on a separate machine;
- evidence-gated queue enforcement.

Want me to continue with the dashboards and rules next? And should I push the aihost commits?

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>" && mkdir -p observability/prometheus/rules observability/prometheus/tests observability/grafana/provisioning observability/grafana/dashboards observability/tools && cat > observability/prometheus/rules/aihost.rules.yml <<'EOF'
# Recording and alerting rules for the aihost inference host.
#
# Metric sources: the orchestrator gateway (`aihost_*`, job "aihost-gateway"), the host textfile exporter
# (`aihost_gpu_*`, via node_exporter) and node_exporter itself (`node_*`, job "node").
#
# Thresholds in the alert group are INITIAL DEFAULTS chosen from this host's observed behaviour, not SLOs;
# revisit them once Prometheus holds a few weeks of history.
groups:
  - name: aihost_recording
    interval: 30s
    rules:
      # ---- engine throughput (the engine's own counters; they advance when a request finishes) ----------
      - record: aihost:engine_decode_tokens_per_second:rate5m
        # Tokens generated per second of *generation time* (decode speed), not per wall-clock second.
        expr: rate(aihost_engine_generation_tokens_total[5m]) / (rate(aihost_engine_generation_seconds_total[5m]) > 0)
      - record: aihost:engine_prompt_eval_tokens_per_second:rate5m
        # Prompt tokens evaluated per second of prompt-processing time (cached tokens excluded).
        expr: rate(aihost_engine_prompt_tokens_total[5m]) / (rate(aihost_engine_prompt_seconds_total[5m]) > 0)
      - record: aihost:engine_prefix_cache_hit_ratio:rate1h
        # Windowed share of prompt tokens served from cache (the exported gauge is a lifetime ratio).
        expr: >-
          rate(aihost_engine_prompt_tokens_cached_total[1h])
          / ((rate(aihost_engine_prompt_tokens_cached_total[1h]) + rate(aihost_engine_prompt_tokens_total[1h])) > 0)

      # ---- gateway requests -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
      - record: aihost:inference_completions:rate5m
        expr: sum by (worker_id, outcome) (rate(aihost_inference_completions_total[5m]))
      - record: aihost:inference_error_ratio:rate5m
        # Provider-side failures only. outcome="rejected" is a caller fault and is deliberately excluded.
        expr: >-
          sum by (worker_id) (rate(aihost_inference_completions_total{outcome=~"failed|timed_out"}[5m]))
          / (sum by (worker_id) (rate(aihost_inference_completions_total{outcome=~"completed|failed|timed_out"}[5m])) > 0)
      - record: aihost:inference_duration_seconds:p50_5m
        expr: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (pool, le) (rate(aihost_inference_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])))
      - record: aihost:inference_duration_seconds:p95_5m
        expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (pool, le) (rate(aihost_inference_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])))
      - record: aihost:inference_tokens_estimated_share:rate1h
        # Share of counted tokens that are the gateway's estimate instead of the engine's exact usage.
        expr: >-
          sum(rate(aihost_inference_prompt_tokens_total{source="estimated"}[1h]) or rate(aihost_inference_completion_tokens_total{source="estimated"}[1h]))
          / (sum(rate(aihost_inference_prompt_tokens_total[1h]) or rate(aihost_inference_completion_tokens_total[1h])) > 0)

      # ---- GPU ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      - record: aihost:gpu_utilization_ratio:rate5m
        # 1 - share of time the graphics tile spent in RC6 idle: "awake", a coarse busy signal (not EU occupancy).
        expr: clamp(1 - rate(aihost_gpu_gt_idle_residency_seconds_total{gt="gt0"}[5m]), 0, 1)
      - record: aihost:gpu_power_watts:rate5m
        expr: sum by (gpu) (rate(aihost_gpu_energy_joules_total{domain="card"}[5m]))
      - record: aihost:joules_per_generated_token_incl_idle:rate15m
        # Whole-card energy over 15 minutes per generated token, idle time included: it falls as utilisation rises.
        expr: >-
          sum by (worker_id) (rate(aihost_gpu_energy_joules_total{domain="card"}[15m]) * on (gpu) group_left (worker_id) aihost_worker_info)
          / (sum by (worker_id) (rate(aihost_engine_generation_tokens_total[15m])) > 0)
      - record: aihost:gpu_temperature_headroom_celsius:min
        # Smallest gap between any sensor and its kernel-reported critical limit, per GPU.
        expr: min by (gpu) (aihost_gpu_temperature_limit_celsius - on (gpu, bdf, sensor) aihost_gpu_temperature_celsius)

      # ---- host CPU: decode is bound by one CPU thread, so the busiest core is the number that matters -----
      - record: aihost:cpu_core_busy_ratio:rate5m
        expr: 1 - rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{mode="idle"}[5m])
      - record: aihost:cpu_busiest_core_ratio:rate5m
        expr: max by (instance) (1 - rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{mode="idle"}[5m]))

  - name: aihost_alerts
    rules:
      - alert: AihostGatewayDown
        expr: up{job="aihost-gateway"} == 0
        for: 2m
        labels: {severity: critical}
        annotations:
          summary: "The orchestrator gateway is not being scraped"
      - alert: AihostMetricsFileStale
        expr: time() - aihost_metrics_last_success_timestamp_seconds > 300
        for: 5m
        labels: {severity: warning}
        annotations:
          summary: "Host GPU metrics have not been refreshed for over 5 minutes (aihost-metrics.timer runs every minute)"
      - alert: AihostWorkerUnhealthy
        expr: aihost_worker_health_status == 0
        for: 2m
        labels: {severity: critical}
        annotations:
          summary: "Worker {{ $labels.worker_id }} is reported unhealthy by the gateway"
      - alert: AihostWorkerEngineStatsMissing
        expr: aihost_worker_health_status == 1 unless on (worker_id) aihost_engine_requests_running
        for: 5m
        labels: {severity: warning}
        annotations:
          summary: "Worker {{ $labels.worker_id }} is healthy but its engine statistics are not being published"
      - alert: AihostInferenceErrorRatioHigh
        expr: >-
          aihost:inference_error_ratio:rate5m > 0.05
          and on (worker_id) sum by (worker_id) (rate(aihost_inference_completions_total[5m])) > 0.01
        for: 10m
        labels: {severity: warning}
        annotations:
          summary: "More than 5% of requests to {{ $labels.worker_id }} are failing on the provider side"
      - alert: AihostRequestsQueueingInEngine
        expr: aihost_engine_requests_waiting > 0
        for: 5m
        labels: {severity: warning}
        annotations:
          summary: "{{ $labels.worker_id }} has requests waiting for a free slot (sustained queueing)"
      - alert: AihostKvCacheNearFull
        expr: aihost_engine_kv_cache_usage_ratio > 0.9
        for: 10m
        labels: {severity: warning}
        annotations:
          summary: "{{ $labels.worker_id }} context occupancy is above 90%"
      - alert: AihostGpuThermalWarning
        expr: aihost_gpu_thermal_severity >= 1
        for: 2m
        labels: {severity: warning}
        annotations:
          summary: "GPU thermal severity is warning or worse (host thresholds)"
      - alert: AihostGpuThermalCritical
        expr: aihost_gpu_thermal_severity >= 2
        for: 1m
        labels: {severity: critical}
        annotations:
          summary: "GPU thermal severity is critical"
      - alert: AihostGpuNearKernelTemperatureLimit
        expr: aihost:gpu_temperature_headroom_celsius:min < 10
        for: 2m
        labels: {severity: critical}
        annotations:
          summary: "GPU {{ $labels.gpu }} is within 10 C of a kernel-reported critical limit"
      - alert: AihostDiskSpaceLow
        expr: >-
          node_filesystem_avail_bytes{mountpoint=~"/|/var/lib/local-ai",fstype!~"tmpfs|overlay"}
          / node_filesystem_size_bytes{mountpoint=~"/|/var/lib/local-ai",fstype!~"tmpfs|overlay"} < 0.10
        for: 15m
        labels: {severity: warning}
        annotations:
          summary: "{{ $labels.mountpoint }} has less than 10% free space"
      - alert: AihostMemoryLow
        expr: node_memory_MemAvailable_bytes / node_memory_MemTotal_bytes < 0.05
        for: 10m
        labels: {severity: warning}
        annotations:
          summary: "Less than 5% of host memory is available"
EOF
~/.local/bin/promtool check rules observability/prometheus/rules/aihost.rules.yml

cat > tools/build_dashboards.py <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate the Grafana dashboards deterministically (so they are reviewable, diffable and testable).

    python observability/tools/build_dashboards.py            # write observability/grafana/dashboards/*.json
    python observability/tools/build_dashboards.py --check    # exit 1 if the committed files differ

Every expression only uses metrics that exist (tests/test_observability_as_code.py enforces that), and every
panel carries a unit and a plain-language description of what it does and does not tell you.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

OUT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "grafana" / "dashboards"
DS = {"type": "prometheus", "uid": "${DS_PROMETHEUS}"}


class Board:
    def __init__(self, uid: str, title: str, description: str):
        self.uid, self.title, self.description = uid, title, description
        self.panels: list[dict] = []
        self._y = 0
        self._x = 0
        self._id = 1

    def row(self, title: str) -> None:
        self._x, self._y = 0, self._y + (0 if not self.panels else 8)
        self.panels.append({"id": self._id, "type": "row", "title": title, "collapsed": False,
                            "gridPos": {"h": 1, "w": 24, "x": 0, "y": self._y}, "panels": []})
        self._id += 1
        self._y += 1

    def _place(self, w: int, h: int) -> dict:
        if self._x + w > 24:
            self._x, self._y = 0, self._y + h
        pos = {"h": h, "w": w, "x": self._x, "y": self._y}
        self._x += w
        return pos

    def _target(self, expr: str, legend: str, ref: str) -> dict:
        return {"datasource": DS, "expr": expr, "legendFormat": legend, "refId": ref, "editorMode": "code", "range": True}

    def timeseries(self, title: str, description: str, targets: list[tuple[str, str]], unit: str = "short",
                   w: int = 12, h: int = 8, stack: bool = False, min_: float | None = None, max_: float | None = None) -> None:
        defaults = {"unit": unit, "custom": {"fillOpacity": 25 if stack else 8, "lineWidth": 1, "showPoints": "never",
                                              "stacking": {"mode": "normal" if stack else "none"}}}
        if min_ is not None:
            defaults["min"] = min_
        if max_ is not None:
            defaults["max"] = max_
        self.panels.append({"id": self._id, "type": "timeseries", "title": title, "description": description, "datasource": DS,
                            "gridPos": self._place(w, h), "fieldConfig": {"defaults": defaults, "overrides": []},
                            "options": {"legend": {"displayMode": "list", "placement": "bottom"}, "tooltip": {"mode": "multi"}},
                            "targets": [self._target(e, l, chr(65 + i)) for i, (e, l) in enumerate(targets)]})
        self._id += 1

    def stat(self, title: str, description: str, expr: str, unit: str = "short", w: int = 6, h: int = 4,
             thresholds: list[tuple[float | None, str]] | None = None) -> None:
        steps = [{"color": c, "value": v} for v, c in (thresholds or [(None, "green")])]
        self.panels.append({"id": self._id, "type": "stat", "title": title, "description": description, "datasource": DS,
                            "gridPos": self._place(w, h),
                            "fieldConfig": {"defaults": {"unit": unit, "thresholds": {"mode": "absolute", "steps": steps}}, "overrides": []},
                            "options": {"reduceOptions": {"calcs": ["lastNotNull"], "fields": "", "values": False}, "colorMode": "value"},
                            "targets": [self._target(expr, "", "A")]})
        self._id += 1

    def build(self) -> dict:
        return {"uid": self.uid, "title": self.title, "description": self.description, "schemaVersion": 39, "version": 1,
                "editable": False, "graphTooltip": 1, "refresh": "30s", "tags": ["aihost"], "time": {"from": "now-6h", "to": "now"},
                "timezone": "browser",
                "templating": {"list": [
                    {"name": "DS_PROMETHEUS", "label": "Prometheus", "type": "datasource", "query": "prometheus", "current": {}, "hide": 0},
                    {"name": "worker", "label": "Worker", "type": "query", "datasource": DS, "includeAll": True, "multi": True,
                     "allValue": ".*", "refresh": 2, "current": {"selected": True, "text": "All", "value": "$__all"},
                     "query": {"query": "label_values(aihost_worker_info, worker_id)", "refId": "worker"}}]},
                "panels": self.panels}


def inference() -> dict:
    b = Board("aihost-inference", "AIHost - inference",
              "Gateway and engine view of the local inference stack. Engine counters advance when a request finishes, "
              "so rates are smooth only over minutes; TTFT and inter-token latency are not measurable (non-streaming upstream).")
    W = 'worker_id=~"$worker"'
    b.row("Overview")
    b.stat("Workers healthy", "Workers the gateway currently considers healthy.", f"sum(aihost_worker_health_status{{{W}}})", thresholds=[(None, "red"), (1, "green")])
    b.stat("Requests / s", "Inference requests received by the gateway.", 'sum(rate(aihost_inference_requests_total{status="received"}[5m]))', unit="reqps")
    b.stat("Provider error ratio", "Failed or timed-out share of requests that reached a worker. Caller faults (rejected) are excluded.",
           f"max(aihost:inference_error_ratio:rate5m{{{W}}}) or vector(0)", unit="percentunit", thresholds=[(None, "green"), (0.05, "red")])
    b.stat("Rejected / s (caller faults)", "Requests refused as invalid for the worker (context overflow, malformed history). Says nothing about worker health.",
           f'sum(rate(aihost_inference_completions_total{{outcome="rejected",{W}}}[5m]))', unit="reqps")
    b.row("Throughput")
    b.timeseries("Decode speed (tokens per busy second)", "Generated tokens divided by generation time, per worker. A decode-speed figure, not wall-clock throughput.",
                 [(f"aihost:engine_decode_tokens_per_second:rate5m{{{W}}}", "{{worker_id}}")], unit="short")
    b.timeseries("Prompt evaluation speed (tokens per busy second)", "Prompt tokens evaluated per second of prompt processing; cached tokens are not included.",
                 [(f"aihost:engine_prompt_eval_tokens_per_second:rate5m{{{W}}}", "{{worker_id}}")], unit="short")
    b.timeseries("Generated tokens / s (wall clock)", "Tokens the engine generated per wall-clock second, averaged over 5 minutes.",
                 [(f"rate(aihost_engine_generation_tokens_total{{{W}}}[5m])", "{{worker_id}}")], unit="short")
    b.timeseries("Prefix-cache hit ratio (1 h window)", "Share of prompt tokens served from cache over the last hour.",
                 [(f"aihost:engine_prefix_cache_hit_ratio:rate1h{{{W}}}", "{{worker_id}}")], unit="percentunit", min_=0, max_=1)
    b.row("Latency")
    b.timeseries("Request duration p50 / p95 by pool", "Time the gateway spent on the worker call, including engine-side queueing. Not time-to-first-token.",
                 [("aihost:inference_duration_seconds:p50_5m", "p50 {{pool}}"), ("aihost:inference_duration_seconds:p95_5m", "p95 {{pool}}")], unit="s")
    b.timeseries("Requests by outcome", "Completed, failed, timed-out and rejected requests per second.",
                 [(f"aihost:inference_completions:rate5m{{{W}}}", "{{worker_id}} {{outcome}}")], unit="reqps", stack=True)
    b.row("Engine state")
    b.timeseries("Running / waiting requests", "Requests being processed and requests deferred inside the engine. Sustained waiting means queueing.",
                 [(f"aihost_engine_requests_running{{{W}}}", "running {{worker_id}}"), (f"aihost_engine_requests_waiting{{{W}}}", "waiting {{worker_id}}")])
    b.timeseries("Context occupancy (KV)", "Share of the context window held by active or retained sequences. When idle this is the retained context, not zero.",
                 [(f"aihost_engine_kv_cache_usage_ratio{{{W}}}", "{{worker_id}}")], unit="percentunit", min_=0, max_=1)
    b.timeseries("In-flight tokens", "Tokens decoded / prompt tokens evaluated so far by requests still running.",
                 [(f"aihost_engine_generation_tokens_in_flight{{{W}}}", "decoded {{worker_id}}"), (f"aihost_engine_prompt_tokens_in_flight{{{W}}}", "prompt {{worker_id}}")])
    b.row("Routing and accounting")
    b.timeseries("Route decisions / s", "Which routing rule sent traffic to which pool.", [("sum by (rule, pool) (rate(aihost_route_decisions_total[5m]))", "{{rule}} -> {{pool}}")],
                 unit="reqps", stack=True)
    b.timeseries("Token accounting by source (tokens / s)", "Tokens the gateway counted: provider = the engine's exact usage, estimated = the gateway's fallback.",
                 [('sum by (source) (rate(aihost_inference_prompt_tokens_total[5m]))', "prompt {{source}}"),
                  ('sum by (source) (rate(aihost_inference_completion_tokens_total[5m]))', "completion {{source}}")], stack=True)
    b.timeseries("Requests outstanding vs configured concurrency", "Requests the gateway has on a worker versus its max concurrency; the excess waits inside the engine.",
                 [(f"aihost_worker_inflight{{{W}}}", "in flight {{worker_id}}"), (f"aihost_worker_max_concurrency{{{W}}}", "max {{worker_id}}")])
    return b.build()


def host() -> dict:
    b = Board("aihost-host", "AIHost - host and GPU",
              "Host CPU, memory, disk and the two Arc GPUs. Decode on this machine is bound by a single CPU thread, so the busiest-core panel "
              "is the one that explains inference speed.")
    b.row("Overview")
    b.stat("Thermal severity", "0 ok, 1 warning, 2 critical, from the host thermal state machine.", "max(aihost_gpu_thermal_severity)", thresholds=[(None, "green"), (1, "orange"), (2, "red")])
    b.stat("Closest GPU temperature to a kernel limit", "Smallest gap (C) between any sensor and its kernel-reported critical limit.", "min(aihost:gpu_temperature_headroom_celsius:min)", unit="celsius",
           thresholds=[(None, "red"), (10, "orange"), (25, "green")])
    b.stat("Busiest CPU core", "Highest per-core busy share over 5 minutes.", "max(aihost:cpu_busiest_core_ratio:rate5m)", unit="percentunit", thresholds=[(None, "green"), (0.9, "orange")])
    b.stat("Host metrics age", "Seconds since the textfile exporter last wrote its file (it runs every minute).", "time() - max(aihost_metrics_last_success_timestamp_seconds)", unit="s",
           thresholds=[(None, "green"), (180, "orange"), (300, "red")])
    b.row("GPU")
    b.timeseries("GPU utilisation (awake share)", "1 minus the share of time the graphics tile sat in RC6 idle: busy or not, not execution-unit occupancy.",
                 [("aihost:gpu_utilization_ratio:rate5m", "gpu{{gpu}}")], unit="percentunit", min_=0, max_=1)

"""Generate the Grafana dashboards deterministically (so they are reviewable, diffable and testable).

    python observability/tools/build_dashboards.py            # write observability/grafana/dashboards/*.json
    python observability/tools/build_dashboards.py --check    # exit 1 if the committed files differ

import json

class Board:
    def __init__(self, uid: str, title: str, description: str):
        self.uid, self.title, self.description = uid, title, description
        self.panels: list[dict] = []
        self._y = 0
        self._x = 0
        self._id = 1

    def row(self, title: str) -> None:
        self._x, self._y = 0, self._y + (0 if not self.panels else 8)
        self.panels.append({"id": self._id, "type": "row", "title": title, "collapsed": False,
                            "gridPos": {"h": 1, "w": 24, "x": 0, "y": self._y}, "panels": []})
        self._id += 1
        self._y += 1

    def _place(self, w: int, h: int) -> dict:
        if self._x + w > 24:
            self._x, self._y = 0, self._y + h
        pos = {"h": h, "w": w, "x": self._x, "y": self._y}
        self._x += w
        return pos

    def _target(self, expr: str, legend: str, ref: str) -> dict:
        return {"datasource": DS, "expr": expr, "legendFormat": legend, "refId": ref, "editorMode": "code", "range": True}

    def timeseries(self, title: str, description: str, targets: list[tuple[str, str]], unit: str = "short",
                   w: int = 12, h: int = 8, stack: bool = False, min_: float | None = None, max_: float | None = None) -> None:
        defaults = {"unit": unit, "custom": {"fillOpacity": 25 if stack else 8, "lineWidth": 1, "showPoints": "never",
                                              "stacking": {"mode": "normal" if stack else "none"}}}
        if min_ is not None:
            defaults["min"] = min_
        if max_ is not None:
            defaults["max"] = max_
        self.panels.append({"id": self._id, "type": "timeseries", "title": title, "description": description, "datasource": DS,
                            "gridPos": self._place(w, h), "fieldConfig": {"defaults": defaults, "overrides": []},
                            "options": {"legend": {"displayMode": "list", "placement": "bottom"}, "tooltip": {"mode": "multi"}},
                            "targets": [self._target(e, l, chr(65 + i)) for i, (e, l) in enumerate(targets)]})
        self._id += 1

    def stat(self, title: str, description: str, expr: str, unit: str = "short", w: int = 6, h: int = 4,
             thresholds: list[tuple[float | None, str]] | None = None) -> None:
        steps = [{"color": c, "value": v} for v, c in (thresholds or [(None, "green")])]
        self.panels.append({"id": self._id, "type": "stat", "title": title, "description": description, "datasource": DS,
                            "gridPos": self._place(w, h),
                            "fieldConfig": {"defaults": {"unit": unit, "thresholds": {"mode": "absolute", "steps": steps}}, "overrides": []},
                            "options": {"reduceOptions": {"calcs": ["lastNotNull"], "fields": "", "values": False}, "colorMode": "value"},
                            "targets": [self._target(expr, "", "A")]})
        self._id += 1

    def build(self) -> dict:
        return {"uid": self.uid, "title": self.title, "description": self.description, "schemaVersion": 39, "version": 1,
                "editable": False, "graphTooltip": 1, "refresh": "30s", "tags": ["aihost"], "time": {"from": "now-6h", "to": "now"},
                "timezone": "browser",
                "templating": {"list": [
                    {"name": "DS_PROMETHEUS", "label": "Prometheus", "type": "datasource", "query": "prometheus", "current": {}, "hide": 0},
                    {"name": "worker", "label": "Worker", "type": "query", "datasource": DS, "includeAll": True, "multi": True,
                     "allValue": ".*", "refresh": 2, "current": {"selected": True, "text": "All", "value": "$__all"},
                     "query": {"query": "label_values(aihost_worker_info, worker_id)", "refId": "worker"}}]},
                "panels": self.panels}

                 [('sum by (source) (rate(aihost_inference_prompt_tokens_total[5m]))', "prompt {{source}}"),

    b.timeseries("Requests outstanding vs configured concurrency", "Requests the gateway has on a worker versus its max concurrency; the excess waits inside the engine.",

content.text:
The dashboards, rules and alerts are committed under `observability/`, and aihost `main` is pushed to origin (`b026041..cfb2097`, 15 commits). The working tree is clean and local matches origin.

**What's in `observability/`**
- **Rules:** 14 recording rules and 12 alerts in one rules file, covering decode speed, prompt speed, windowed prefix hit ratio, provider error ratio, p50/p95 latency by pool, GPU utilization and power, energy per token, temperature headroom to the kernel limit, and busiest CPU core.
- **Alert thresholds:** they are labelled initial defaults to revisit once there's history; I didn't invent SLOs.
- **Dashboards:** two Grafana dashboards (inference, and host/GPU), generated by a script so they're reviewable and diffable. Each panel has a unit and a plain-language description of what it does and doesn't tell you.
- **Example config:** a Prometheus config and Grafana provisioning, all marked as examples and not deployed.

**How it's verified**
- **Unit tests:** 14 `promtool` unit tests with hand-derived numbers. A mutation check confirmed they catch deliberately broken rules, and the new tests fail against the previous versions of the two rules I fixed.
- **pytest checks:** every metric a rule or panel references must exist and actually be emitted, every recording rule must be used, every alert needs severity, summary and a `for:`, and the committed dashboards must match the generator.
- **Live evaluation:** I ran a throwaway Prometheus on this machine for two runs of about 2.5 minutes each, scraping the live gateway and node_exporter through SSH tunnels under real load, then tore it down. All 26 rules evaluated with no errors, and the values match what I measured by hand (decode 22 tok/s on the 27B and 88 tok/s on the lead). Peak in-flight 2, engine waiting 1 and the 94% / 80% prefix hit ratios all show up.

**Defects the live run found**
- The error-ratio and estimated-share rules returned no data in the healthy case, because the numerator series doesn't exist when nothing has failed. They now read 0, and tests guard it.
- `aihost_worker_info` wasn't deployed yet, so the energy-per-token join was empty. I deployed gateway release `b4051cc`, and the join works.

**Findings for you**
- **Energy per generated token** (idle included): **1.6 J on the lead vs 9.0 J on the 27B**, about 5.7× more. That's a concrete number for the routing trade-off.
- **GPU 1's VRAM reached 78 °C** under sustained 27B generation (kernel limit 105 °C), tripping the thermal warning at 75 °C. The alert log named the sensor (`gpu1/vram_ch_5`). This corrects my earlier claim that loads stayed in the 60s–70s.

**Decision for you:** the 75/85 thresholds are fine for the package but conservative for VRAM, which has 27 °C of headroom at 78 °C. I'd set separate VRAM thresholds (say warn 85, critical 95) while keeping the package at 75/85. First I'd check how the benchmarking role reads its 90 °C abort guardrail, so alerts still fire before it. Do you want that?

`promtool` is only a test-time dependency on this machine (checksum-verified install). The pytest checks skip if it's absent.

Remaining from my list: streaming from workers through the gateway, standing up Prometheus on a separate machine, and evidence-gated queue enforcement.

<pasted_content id="bd2e">
I would not change the VRAM alert threshold yet
You are right not to simply make 85/95 the new thresholds because the kernel reports 105°C.
The current 75°C warning firing at 78°C isn't necessarily a defect. A warning is supposed to give operational headroom. Before changing it, I would want to know what the existing benchmark/qualification guardrail actually means, especially the referenced 90°C abort point.
More importantly, we now need to distinguish:
GPU package temperature from VRAM temperature.
They have different thermal characteristics and potentially different operational limits. Using one 75/85 policy for both because both happen to be measured in °C isn't necessarily justified.
So I'd authorize the proposed read-only investigation of the existing 90°C benchmark guardrail, but not threshold changes yet. Establish where 90 came from, what sensor(s) it applies to, and whether there's existing Intel/device evidence or previous qualification behind it. Then decide package and VRAM thresholds separately.
I would also resist the remaining scope creep
Of the three things on the your remaining list:
Streaming from workers through the gateway may be worthwhile if this is an existing functional deficiency with demonstrated user/workload impact. But it isn't inherently an observability task.
Standing up Prometheus on another machine is reasonable eventually, but the current work has already established that the metrics/rules/dashboard artifacts can operate with Prometheus. I wouldn't let permanent monitoring infrastructure become a prerequisite for declaring this observability work successful.
Evidence-gated queue enforcement is a control-plane feature. That's significantly different from observability and should not quietly become part of this task just because queue telemetry now exists. We should first accumulate evidence about real queue behavior before allowing measurements to drive enforcement.
</pasted_content id="bd2e">

---DOC
labeled series (`aihost_gpu_temperature_celsius{device="hwmon1/xe"}`) plus an
unlabeled cross-device peak. The thermal gate in benchmark fixtures reads the
peak across both devices, so neither card can hide a hotspot behind the other's
nominal temperature.

The metrics writer also runs a debounced **GPU thermal severity guard**
(`aihost_gpu_thermal_severity` 0/1/2 from ok/warning/critical). Thresholds
default to `monitoring_gpu_temp_warn_threshold_c: 75` and
`monitoring_gpu_temp_crit_threshold_c: 85` — deliberately below the benchmark
abort guardrail (`benchmarking_abort_temperature_c: 90`) so an operator is
alerted before a workload would be killed. A critical transition is written to
the alert log and forwarded through `AIHOST_ALERT_COMMAND` on both GPU cards'
behalf with context `state=critical temperature_c=<peak>`; recovery to ok after
critical logs a `state=recovered` line.

**Scheduled drift alerting**: `aihost-reconcile.timer` runs the snapshot runner
for `site.yml --validate-after-site` and then a second snapshot run for
`drift-check.yml`, so every scheduled reconciliation classifies drift.
`playbooks/drift-check.yml` raises an operator alert through the local alert
hook when classification is `blocking_drift` or `unknown_drift`, passing the
classification as alert context. Drift is classified fail-closed: a missing or
---TEST

content.text:
The 90 °C abort has no evidence behind it. It's a placeholder default, and nothing in the repo or on the host supports or contradicts it. I changed no thresholds. I left streaming, a separate Prometheus host and queue enforcement alone, as you said. The only edit is a docs fix, committed locally as `63568bd`.

**Where 90 came from**
- It was added on 2026-08-22 in commit `3313544`, "real-mode benchmark harness with thermal and power guardrails," as `benchmarking_abort_temperature_c: 90`. The commit message gives no rationale and cites no Intel or device document.
- The same commit's PSU and TDP defaults (1000 W, 225 W) were generic. This host overrides them to 950 W and 200 W, but the abort temperature was never revisited, despite a comment saying the guardrails were tuned to this host.
- The repo contains no thermal specification for the B65 anywhere. A contract test only requires `warn < crit < abort`, so 90 anchors the monitoring thresholds without ever having been justified.

**What it applies to**
- The abort check takes the hottest of every temperature sensor on each GPU (package, VRAM, memory controller, PCIe, all VRAM channels). It aborts on any single one-second sample at or above 90 °C, with no averaging or debounce.
- Nowhere in the repo is there a package-versus-VRAM distinction, as you suspected: the abort, the benchmark matrix and the original monitoring alert all treat them identically.

**Evidence that exists**
- **Past benchmark runs:** 126 recorded runs peaked at 42–64 °C, and none ever aborted. They were all the old vLLM runs, where decode was CPU-bound and the GPUs lightly loaded, so they say nothing about llama.cpp load or about whether 90 is right.
- **Device-reported limits:**

| Sensor | critical | emergency | other |
|---|---|---|---|
| package | 100 °C | 125 °C | `max` 60 °C |
| VRAM | 105 °C | 120 °C | no `max` |
| memory controller, PCIe | 100 °C | 125 °C | |

  The package `max = 60 °C` is unexplained. The package reached 66 °C with no thermal throttling, so it isn't a throttle point. I couldn't find documentation for it, so I'm not treating it as a limit.
- **Throttle behavior, measured live over 100 seconds of sustained load on both workers:**
  - GPU 0 (lead) peaked at 55 °C package and 58 °C VRAM, with no throttling and frequency steady at 2400 MHz.
  - GPU 1 (27B) peaked at 66 °C package and 72 °C VRAM. Over a longer run earlier, VRAM reached 78 °C.
  - **No thermal throttle flag was ever raised.**
  - GPU 1 did show **power-limit (PL2) throttling** in 60 of 90 samples, dropping frequency only to 2333 MHz (about 3%). It's a power effect, not a thermal one.

**My read:** no evidence says 75 °C is too low or too high for either sensor class. The hardware shows no thermal pressure through 78 °C on VRAM, so the 75 °C VRAM warning fires during normal 27B inference without anything to act on. I'd still hold the thresholds until there's a longer soak.

**Proposed next step (not started):** a 30–60 minute sustained soak of both workers, sampling every sensor and every throttle flag. It would show where VRAM and package temperatures plateau and whether any thermal throttling ever appears. Then the package and VRAM thresholds, and the 90 °C guardrail, can be set from that data together with the kernel limits. It generates sustained GPU load, so I want your go-ahead first.

The doc fix: `docs/observability.md` still described the old unlabeled series and the removed aggregate, which went stale when I rewrote the exporter. It now describes the per-sensor series, the kernel limits and the stricter-only rule.

I did not look up Intel's published thermal specification for the B65. I can try if you want external evidence on top of what the device reports.

message.content:
<pasted_content id="bd2e">
Claude's conclusion is appropriately conservative. The investigation has now established something more important than whether 75°C is "right": **the existing thermal policy has no demonstrated engineering basis.**

The evidence separates into three categories. The 90°C benchmark abort is historical configuration, not a qualified limit. The kernel/device readings provide actual sensor-specific critical/emergency values, but those are protection limits rather than necessarily desirable operating thresholds. And the live tests establish observed behavior under the present llama.cpp workload: approximately 55/58°C package/VRAM on the lead GPU, 66/72°C on the 27B GPU during the >100-second test, with an earlier 78°C VRAM observation and no thermal throttling. The observed throttling was PL2 power limiting, not thermal limiting.

That makes Claude's refusal to change thresholds correct. In particular, I agree with rejecting my earlier suggestion that something like 85/95 might be reasonable. We now have better evidence, and there is no basis yet for selecting those numbers either.

### I would authorize the 30–60 minute soak

This is a case where additional investigation is justified because it resolves a concrete engineering question. The short test hasn't established thermal equilibrium. The important measurement isn't another instantaneous peak, but the **temperature curve and eventual plateau under sustained representative load**.

I would make the experiment slightly more rigorous than simply "run both GPUs for an hour." Have Claude preserve per-sensor time series for package, VRAM channels, memory controller and PCIe, along with GPU utilization, frequency, power, PL1/PL2 state, thermal-throttle flags, fan data if exposed, inference throughput, and ambient/intake temperature if the host exposes anything credible. Sampling at one second is appropriate given the current abort mechanism.

The workload should be stable enough to distinguish warm-up from steady state. The analysis should identify whether each relevant sensor reaches an apparent plateau, its peak, sustained range near the end, and whether throughput/frequency changes correlate with thermal or power throttling. **Do not intentionally drive the hardware toward the reported critical limits.** This is normal sustained inference characterization, not thermal stress-to-failure testing.

I would also have it evaluate the current 90°C abort behavior separately. The finding that **one sample from any sensor trips the entire benchmark** deserves examination independent of the numeric threshold. A single noisy VRAM-channel reading probably should not automatically have identical semantics to sustained package overheating. Sensor-specific thresholds plus a short persistence/debounce policy may eventually be better, but the soak should gather evidence before designing that.

### One thing I would add before setting final thresholds

Claude should look up Intel's published B65 thermal documentation now. Not because the device-reported limits are invalid, but because we're about to turn measurements into operational policy. That's exactly when external authoritative evidence has high information value.

The resulting evidence hierarchy would be strong:

**Intel specification + device-reported protection limits + actual sustained behavior in this exact T5820 + operational margin → monitoring/abort policy.**

If Intel doesn't publish sufficiently specific VRAM/package guidance, record that as unresolved rather than deriving a magic number.

There's also a useful discovery in the power data. GPU1 spent 60/90 samples under PL2 limiting while losing only about 3% clock. That's not necessarily a problem, but it's a real characteristic of this configuration. I wouldn't optimize it now. Preserve it as an observation so future performance/power tuning has a baseline.

And Claude followed the scope instruction correctly: streaming, permanent Prometheus infrastructure, and queue enforcement were left alone; only the stale observability documentation was corrected. That's the right stopping discipline.

So my authorization would be: **proceed with the bounded sustained thermal soak and Intel specification research; make no threshold or guardrail changes during data collection.** Afterward, we review the measurements and decide separately on package warning/critical, VRAM warning/critical, benchmark abort threshold, and persistence/debounce semantics. That would turn the current placeholders into evidence-backed operating policy rather than simply replacing one set of guesses with another.
</pasted_content id="bd2e">

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead. claude.ai artifact links (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) are published artifacts: read them with the Artifact tool (action "read"), not WebFetch or curl.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

# Intel Xe hwmon Attributes Summary

## Temperature Attributes

**temp2_input (Package):** "RO. Package temperature in millidegree Celsius."

**temp2_max:** "RO. Package maximum temperature limit in millidegree Celsius." (Document does not specify function like throttling threshold)

**temp2_crit:** "RO. Package critical temperature in millidegree Celsius." (Document does not specify if this is a throttle threshold or shutdown trigger)

**temp2_emergency:** "RO. Package shutdown temperature in millidegree Celsius."

**temp3_input (VRAM):** "RO. VRAM temperature in millidegree Celsius."

**temp3_crit:** "RO. VRAM critical temperature in millidegree Celsius." (Function not specified in document)

**temp3_emergency:** "RO. VRAM shutdown temperature in millidegree Celsius."

**temp4_input (Memory Controller):** "RO. Memory controller average temperature in millidegree Celsius."

**temp4_crit:** "RO. Memory controller critical temperature in millidegree Celsius." (Function not specified)

**temp4_emergency:** "RO. Memory controller shutdown temperature in millidegree Celsius."

**temp5_input (GPU PCIe):** "RO. GPU PCIe temperature in millidegree Celsius."

**temp5_crit & temp5_emergency:** "RO. GPU PCIe critical/shutdown temperature in millidegree Celsius."

**temp[6-21]_input (VRAM Channels):** "RO. VRAM channel temperature in millidegree Celsius."

**temp[6-21]_crit & temp[6-21]_emergency:** "RO. VRAM channel critical/shutdown temperature in millidegree Celsius."

## Fan Attributes

**fan1_input, fan2_input, fan3_input:** "RO. Fan [1-3] speed in RPM."

## Energy/Power Attributes

**energy1_input:** "RO. Card energy input of device in microjoules."

**energy2_input:** "RO. Package energy input of device in microjoules."

**power1_max:** "RW. Card reactive sustained (PL1) power limit in microwatts."

**power1_max_interval:** "RW. Card sustained power limit interval (Tau in PL1/Tau) in milliseconds."

**power1_cap:** "RW. Card burst (PL2) power limit in microwatts."

**power1_cap_interval:** "RW. Card burst power limit interval (Tau in PL2/Tau) in milliseconds."

**power1_crit:** "RW. Card reactive critical (I1) power limit in microwatts."

**power2_max:** "RW. Package reactive sustained (PL1) power limit in microwatts."

**power2_cap:** "RW. Package burst (PL2) power limit in microwatts."

**power2_cap_interval:** "RW. Package burst power limit interval (Tau in PL2/Tau) in milliseconds."

**power2_max_interval:** "RW. Package sustained power limit interval (Tau in PL1/Tau) in milliseconds."

**curr1_crit:** "RW. Card reactive critical (I1) power limit in milliamperes."

**in1_input:** "RO. Package current voltage in millivolt."

content.text:
The soak is waiting for the GPUs to cool to a clean starting point (44 °C now, target 34 °C, capped at 15 minutes). After that it records for about 54 minutes. I'm not touching the host in the meantime.

**Intel research (complete), including what I could not find**

| Source | Thermal content |
|---|---|
| [Intel ARK, Arc Pro B65](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/products/sku/245796/intel-arc-pro-b65-graphics/specifications.html) | only **TBP 200 W** |
| [Intel B65 datasheet v1.0](https://www.intel.com/content/dam/www/central-libraries/us/en/documents/2026-03/datasheet-b65-gpu.pdf) (3 pages, text extracted) | 200 W total board power; no temperature limit |
| Intel B-series quick-reference guide | no thermal content |
| [Intel B60 GPU management guide](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/860316/REDACTED.4.pdf) | reports GPU-core and memory temperatures separately and lets an operator set a throttle-threshold policy, but gives no default limits |
| [Intel support article on Arc overheating](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/support/articles/000094044/graphics.html) | only says users observe GPU and VRAM temperatures "over 90 Celsius" while gaming. It states no threshold or throttle behavior, and it covers A-series gaming cards. |
| [ASRock Creator 32GB spec page](https://www.asrock.com/Graphics-Card/Intel/Intel%20Arc%20Pro%20B65%20Creator%2032GB/index.us.asp) (our boards are ASRock, subsystem 1849:6027) | no temperature or thermal fields |
| [Kernel `sysfs-driver-intel-xe-hwmon` ABI](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/master/Documentation/ABI/testing/sysfs-driver-intel-xe-hwmon) (read via the fetch tool's summary) | `emergency` is the **shutdown** temperature. `crit` is "critical temperature" with no stated function. `temp2_max` is "package maximum temperature limit," also with no stated function. `power1_cap` is the **PL2** burst limit. |

**Result:** Intel publishes **no** thermal limit, junction limit, memory limit or throttle point for the B65. I'm recording that as unresolved publicly, not deriving a number from it. The usable authoritative evidence is the device-reported values (emergency = shutdown, per the kernel doc) plus what the soak measures.

I'll report the soak when it finishes, with the full analysis and the evidence package preserved. It will be per-sensor curves, plateau and range per sensor, throttle duty cycles, throughput against temperature, the single-sample noise analysis for the abort behavior, and the PL2 baseline.

cat > README.md <<'EOF'
# Sustained-inference thermal soak (2026-10-03)

Question: what do the two Arc Pro B65 GPUs actually do thermally under *sustained, representative* llama.cpp inference on
this Dell Precision 5820 (Xeon W-2123, BIOS 2.51.1, kernel 7.0.0-34), and does anything justify the current thermal
policy (monitoring warning 75 C / critical 85 C, benchmark abort 90 C)?

**No threshold or guardrail was changed by this work.** It is evidence collection; the policy decisions are listed at the end.

## Method
- One 54-minute run through the gateway aliases `engineering/lead` (GPU 0, Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B Q4_K_M) and `engineering/deep`
  (GPU 1, Qwen3.5-27B Q4_K_M), both GPUs loaded the whole time, closed-loop (next request starts when the last ends).
- Phases: 120 s idle baseline -> **decode-heavy 1320 s** (short prompt, 1500/700 generated tokens) -> **prefill-heavy 1320 s**
  (unique ~14k-token prompts, the mean agent context on this host, no cache reuse) -> 480 s cooldown. Started from a cool
  state (all GPU sensors <= 34 C).
- 1 Hz recording of every GPU sensor (20 per card), energy, graphics-tile idle residency, actual frequency, every throttle
  flag, GPU fan; host CPU temperatures/load, chassis fans, NVMe, five unlabeled `dell_smm` temperatures; per-request
  throughput; gateway engine metrics every 10 s.
- Safety: load would have stopped at 90 C on any GPU sensor (the existing guardrail, used only as a stop). It never tripped.
  The soak was not intended to approach the reported critical limits and did not.
- Not evidence: a 65 s dry run of the instrument (discarded) and three earlier short probes (GPU-to-worker mapping, a 100 s
  load, a prefill sizing request).

## Results (all from `analysis/analyze.py`; tables in `analysis/analysis_output.txt`, curves in `analysis/plots/`)

**Equilibrium.** Every sensor reached a plateau: 90% of the rise within 83-189 s of load start, and the last-5-minute slope of
every sensor is within +-0.14 C/min. The 22-minute phases are at thermal steady state.

| Steady state (last 5 min of phase), C | decode | prefill | peak (whole run) | idle |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GPU 0 package | 66.0 (63-66) | 65.2 (62-67) | 67 | 30 |
| GPU 0 VRAM (hottest channel) | 76.0 (74-76) | 72.3 (70-74) | 76 | 32 |
| GPU 1 package | 69.0 (66-70) | 69.0 (63-70) | 70 | 31 |
| GPU 1 VRAM (hottest channel) | **82.6 (80-84)** | 79.9 (74-80) | **84** | 34 |
| memory controller / PCIe | 49-51 / 67-69 | 49-51 / 66-69 | 51 / 70 | 23 / 32 |

Decode (memory-bound) runs the VRAM 2.7-3.7 C hotter than prefill. The `vram` sensor equals the hottest of the 16 channels; the
hottest channel reads **6.0 C (GPU 0) / 8.2 C (GPU 1) above the median channel** at the decode plateau.

**Margins on the hottest observation.** GPU 1 VRAM peak 84 C is 21 C below the kernel `crit` (105), 36 C below the shutdown
`emergency` (120), 6 C below the 90 C benchmark abort and **1 C below the current 85 C critical**. Package peak 70 C is 30 C
below its `crit` (100).

**Throttling.** In 3,244 samples on both GPUs **no thermal flag was ever raised** (`thermal`, `prochot`, `vr_thermalert`,
`ratl` all zero). The only flag is **PL2 power limiting on GPU 1: 2,482 samples, about 96% of loaded time**; card power sits
at 198 W (cap 200 W) and the actual frequency runs at a median 2333 MHz in decode and 2250 MHz in prefill against 2400 MHz
(-2.8% / -6.3%), constant from the first minute. GPU 0 draws about 141 W and never throttles. **Throughput is flat over each
22-minute phase** (decode: lead 83.1 -> 83.6 tok/s, deep 21.5 -> 21.6; prefill: lead 1212 -> 1209, deep 759 -> 759;
|Spearman(rate, temperature)| <= 0.19; 0 failed requests): no temperature-related performance change was observed.

**Against the current policy (informational).** VRAM >= 75 C for **39% (GPU 0) and 95.5% (GPU 1) of the loaded time**, so the
75 C warning is effectively an "inference is running" signal, while the 85 C critical was never reached (peak 84 C).

**Single-sample behaviour (the abort evidence).** Sensors have 1 C resolution. Isolated one-sample upward excursions >= 2 C
occur in 0.66% (GPU 0) / 0.81% (GPU 1) of VRAM channel-samples and **never exceed +2 C**; larger sample-to-sample jumps are real
transitions. So noise is small; the issue is proximity. What a threshold T with persistence N seconds would have done to the
hottest sensor in the loaded phases (separate trips):

| | N=1 s | 3 | 5 | 10 | 30 | 60 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GPU 0, T=75 C | 17 | 15 | 14 | 14 | 9 | 7 |
| GPU 1, T=75 C | 10 | 10 | 10 | 10 | 10 | 6 |
| GPU 1, T=80 C | 47 | 46 | 45 | 44 | 20 | 1 |
| T=85 C or 90 C (either GPU) | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

**Cooling and host.** The hottest sensor loses 50% of its excess in 63-92 s and 90% in 346-379 s. GPU fans: GPU 0 idles at
about 1080 rpm and runs 1680; GPU 1 **idles at 0 rpm** and runs 2400-2460. During load the busiest CPU core is at **98%**
with total CPU at 28% (the single-thread bottleneck persists under llama.cpp). Ambient: no labeled sensor; `dell_smm` `temp5`
read a constant 25.0 C and `temp7` rose 26.2 -> 28.0 C, so the room was probably about 25-28 C. **Identity unverified.**

## Caveats and limits
- One soak, one ambient (about 25-28 C, unverified), llama.cpp workloads only, two 22-minute phases. Nothing here says what
  happens at higher ambient or lower airflow; no extrapolation is made.
- `temp2_max = 60 C` on the package is unexplained (exceeded by 6-10 C with no throttle flag).
- Data quality: `act_freq` reads 0 at request boundaries (medians used); a few `dell_smm` fan readings are missing (counted in
  `summary.json`); the GPU fan trace shows brief dips (medians used, 0 dropouts below 300 rpm while loaded).
- Intel/board-vendor documentation publishes no thermal limits: see `research/intel-thermal-documentation.md`.

## Decisions deliberately not taken (to be made from this evidence)
1. Package warning/critical. 2. VRAM warning/critical (separately). 3. The 90 C benchmark abort value and which sensors it
applies to. 4. Persistence/debounce semantics. 5. Whether to record the GPU 1 PL2 limiting (about 6% clock cost in prefill)
as a baseline for later power tuning (preserved here as an observation only).

## Layout
`raw/` original host files + `host-sha256.txt` (verified identical after copy) | `analysis/analyze.py`, `plots.py`,
`summary.json`, `analysis_output.txt`, `plots/` | `research/` | `SHA256SUMS`.
EOF

**Margins on the hottest observation.** GPU 1 VRAM peak 84 C is 21 C below the kernel `crit` (105), 36 C below the shutdown
`emergency` (120), 6 C below the 90 C benchmark abort and **1 C below the current 85 C critical**. Package peak 70 C is 30 C
below its `crit` (100).

**Throttling.** In 3,244 samples on both GPUs **no thermal flag was ever raised** (`thermal`, `prochot`, `vr_thermalert`,
`ratl` all zero). The only flag is **PL2 power limiting on GPU 1: 2,482 samples, about 96% of loaded time**; card power sits
at 198 W (cap 200 W) and the actual frequency runs at a median 2333 MHz in decode and 2250 MHz in prefill against 2400 MHz
(-2.8% / -6.3%), constant from the first minute. GPU 0 draws about 141 W and never throttles. **Throughput is flat over each
22-minute phase** (decode: lead 83.1 -> 83.6 tok/s, deep 21.5 -> 21.6; prefill: lead 1212 -> 1209, deep 759 -> 759;
|Spearman(rate, temperature)| <= 0.19; 0 failed requests): no temperature-related performance change was observed.

**Against the current policy (informational).** VRAM >= 75 C for **39% (GPU 0) and 95.5% (GPU 1) of the loaded time**, so the
75 C warning is effectively an "inference is running" signal, while the 85 C critical was never reached (peak 84 C).

**Single-sample behaviour (the abort evidence).** Sensors have 1 C resolution. Isolated one-sample upward excursions >= 2 C
occur in 0.66% (GPU 0) / 0.81% (GPU 1) of VRAM channel-samples and **never exceed +2 C**; larger sample-to-sample jumps are real
transitions. So noise is small; the issue is proximity. What a threshold T with persistence N seconds would have done to the
hottest sensor in the loaded phases (separate trips):

| | N=1 s | 3 | 5 | 10 | 30 | 60 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GPU 0, T=75 C | 17 | 15 | 14 | 14 | 9 | 7 |
| GPU 1, T=75 C | 10 | 10 | 10 | 10 | 10 | 6 |
| GPU 1, T=80 C | 47 | 46 | 45 | 44 | 20 | 1 |
| T=85 C or 90 C (either GPU) | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

**Cooling and host.** The hottest sensor loses 50% of its excess in 63-92 s and 90% in 346-379 s. GPU fans: GPU 0 idles at
about 1080 rpm and runs 1680; GPU 1 **idles at 0 rpm** and runs 2400-2460. During load the busiest CPU core is at **98%**
with total CPU at 28% (the single-thread bottleneck persists under llama.cpp). Ambient: no labeled sensor; `dell_smm` `temp5`
read a constant 25.0 C and `temp7` rose 26.2 -> 28.0 C, so the room was probably about 25-28 C. **Identity unverified.**

- One soak, one ambient (about 25-28 C, unverified), llama.cpp workloads only, two 22-minute phases. Nothing here says what
  happens at higher ambient or lower airflow; no extrapolation is made.
- `temp2_max = 60 C` on the package is unexplained (exceeded by 6-10 C with no throttle flag).
- Data quality: `act_freq` reads 0 at request boundaries (medians used); a few `dell_smm` fan readings are missing (counted in

- Intel/board-vendor documentation publishes no thermal limits: see `research/intel-thermal-documentation.md`.

## Decisions deliberately not taken (to be made from this evidence)
1. Package warning/critical. 2. VRAM warning/critical (separately). 3. The 90 C benchmark abort value and which sensors it
applies to. 4. Persistence/debounce semantics. 5. Whether to record the GPU 1 PL2 limiting (about 6% clock cost in prefill)
as a baseline for later power tuning (preserved here as an observation only).

content.text:
The soak ran cleanly and its evidence is preserved in the Nexus repo, committed locally as `1b177cb` and not pushed. No threshold or guardrail was changed, and the safety stop at 90 °C never tripped.

**Run:** a 54-minute run on both GPUs: a 2-minute idle baseline, then a 22-minute decode-heavy phase, a 22-minute phase of unique ~14k-token prompts (the mean agent context), and an 8-minute cooldown. It started from a cool state (all sensors ≤34 °C). It recorded every sensor (20 per card) at 1 Hz, plus energy, frequency, every throttle flag, fans, host data and per-request throughput.

**Equilibrium:** every sensor reached a plateau (90% of the rise within 83–189 s) with last-5-minute slopes within ±0.14 °C/min. So the 22-minute phases are at steady state, not another instantaneous peak.

| Steady-state, °C (decode) | Package | VRAM (hottest channel) | Peak VRAM |
|---|---|---|---|
| GPU 0 (lead) | 66 | 76 | 76 |
| GPU 1 (27B) | 69 | **82.6 (80–84)** | **84** |

- **Prefill vs decode:** VRAM runs 2.7–3.7 °C cooler in prefill (GPU 1: 79.9, GPU 0: 72.3), since decode is memory-bound.
- **Margins:** GPU 1's peak VRAM of 84 °C is 21 °C below the kernel `crit` (105), 36 °C below the shutdown limit (120), 6 °C below the benchmark abort and **1 °C below the current 85 °C critical**. Package peak is 70 °C, 30 °C below its `crit` (100).
- **No thermal throttling, ever.** The `thermal`, `prochot`, `vr_thermalert` and `ratl` flags were zero in all 3,244 samples on both GPUs.
- **PL2 power limiting on GPU 1:** raised in 94.0% of its loaded samples (96% decode, 92% prefill), with frequency at a median 2333 MHz in decode and 2250 MHz in prefill against 2400 MHz (−2.8% and −6.3%). It's preserved as a baseline observation for later power tuning. GPU 0 draws about 141 W and never throttles.
- **Throughput is flat** over each phase (lead 83.1 → 83.6 tok/s decode and 1,212 → 1,209 prefill; deep 21.5 → 21.6 and 759 → 759; 0 failed requests), so no temperature-related slowdown was observed.

**The one-sample abort**
- **Noise isn't the issue.** Sensors have 1 °C resolution. Isolated one-sample upward spikes occur in under 1% of VRAM channel-samples and never exceed +2 °C.
- **Proximity is.** The single-sample behavior matters because GPU 1's plateau sits near any candidate threshold. At 80 °C, GPU 1 would have tripped 47 times with no persistence, 20 times with 30 s and once with 60 s. At 85 or 90 °C, nothing trips with any persistence.
- **The `vram` sensor is the hottest of 16 channels.** At the decode plateau it reads 6.0 °C (GPU 0) and 8.2 °C (GPU 1) above the median channel, so "max of all sensors" tracks the hottest GDDR channel.
- **Against the current policy:** VRAM was at or above the 75 °C warning for 39% (GPU 0) and 95.5% (GPU 1) of loaded time, so the warning mostly means "inference is running."

**Intel documentation:** no thermal limit, junction limit, memory limit or throttle point is published for the B65. I checked Intel's ARK page, the B65 datasheet (text extracted in full), the quick-reference guide, the B60 management guide, Intel's Arc overheating support article and ASRock's spec table. I recorded this as unresolved and derived no number from it. The kernel ABI confirms `emergency` is the shutdown temperature and `power1_cap` is the PL2 limit. The ABI summary came through a fetch tool's summarization, not the raw text. Details are in `research/intel-thermal-documentation.md`.

**Caveats**
- One soak at one ambient. No labeled ambient sensor exists; unlabeled `dell_smm` readings suggest about 25–28 °C, identity unverified.
- No extrapolation to a warmer room or lower airflow.
- `temp2_max = 60 °C` on the package remains unexplained.
- A few readings are missing or zero (GPU fan dips, a missing fan reading), handled with medians and disclosed.
- During load the busiest CPU core sat at 98% with total CPU at 28%, so the single-thread bottleneck persists under llama.cpp.

**Decisions still open, as you listed them:** package warning and critical, VRAM warning and critical (separately), the benchmark abort value and which sensors it applies to, and the persistence/debounce semantics. The data above is the input. I've proposed no numbers.

<pasted_content id="bd2e">
This is a much stronger result than the point observations suggested, because Claude now has enough longitudinal data to distinguish transient values from sustained behavior.

The most important result is not the peak temperatures. It is the combination of **thermal equilibrium + stable throughput + zero thermal-throttle indications**. Both 22-minute loaded phases apparently reached equilibrium quickly, with 90% of the temperature rise occurring within 83–189 seconds and last-five-minute slopes within ±0.14 °C/min. If those calculations reproduce from the raw samples, that is strong evidence that we were observing steady-state behavior within this tested envelope, rather than temperatures that were still climbing when the experiment ended.

The actual operating points are also useful. Decode steady state was about **66°C package / 76°C hottest VRAM on GPU0**, and **69°C package / 82.6°C hottest VRAM on GPU1**, with GPU1 peaking at 84°C VRAM. Prefill ran several degrees cooler despite the enormous prompt throughput we saw. Most importantly, Claude reports **zero thermal, prochot, VR thermal, and RATL flags across all 3,244 samples on both GPUs**, while throughput remained essentially flat across each phase.

That materially strengthens the proposition:

> **Within this workload, ambient condition, hardware configuration and observation period, the T5820 cooling system reached a thermal equilibrium while both GPUs sustained useful inference without observed thermal throttling or temperature-correlated throughput degradation.**

That's a defensible conclusion. It says nothing about warmer rooms, restricted airflow, different workloads, component aging, or maximum safe temperatures.

### The surprising result is GPU1's PL2 behavior

GPU1 apparently asserted PL2 power limiting for **94% of loaded samples**, while GPU0 never did. Yet GPU1's frequency remained around 2333 MHz during decode versus 2400 MHz nominal, only about 2.8% lower, and throughput remained stable.

That's potentially much more interesting for future optimization than thermals.

It doesn't yet establish that increasing or changing power limits would improve useful performance. It establishes that **the 27B workload is routinely encountering a power-control boundary before encountering a thermal-control boundary** under this test.

That's exactly the kind of thing this experiment was supposed to uncover. We started asking a thermal question and discovered another potentially relevant operating constraint. No reason to tune it yet. Preserve it as the next hypothesis.

### The current 75°C VRAM warning has now been experimentally characterized

This is particularly clear.

During loaded operation, VRAM was at or above 75°C for **39% of GPU0's loaded samples and 95.5% of GPU1's**. Yet there was no corresponding thermal throttling, throughput degradation, failure, or inability to reach equilibrium.

So Claude's wording that the existing warning largely means *“inference is running”* is directionally fair for this workload.

That doesn't prove 75°C is universally safe or tell us what the replacement threshold should be. It demonstrates that **75°C is poorly discriminating as an operational warning for this qualified workload**.

And Claude correctly did **not** change it.

### The abort analysis uncovered a design issue separate from temperature selection

The current benchmark safety mechanism appears to use the hottest reading from all temperature sensors and abort on a single sample.

The soak suggests that sensor selection may actually be reasonable in one respect: the maximum VRAM reading tracks the hottest physical GDDR channel, which is meaningfully hotter than the median. We shouldn't average that away.

But **single-sample threshold semantics** are a separate question.

At an 80°C threshold, GPU1 would apparently have generated 47 aborts with no persistence requirement, despite only 20 excursions lasting ≥30 seconds and one lasting ≥60 seconds. At 85°C or 90°C, none occurred.

So there are really at least three independent policy decisions here:

```text
WHAT is measured?
    package / hottest VRAM / other sensors

WHAT does the threshold mean?
    warning / critical / protective abort

HOW must it occur?
    instantaneous / persistence / hysteresis / combination
```

Those shouldn't be collapsed into one temperature number.

### Intel documentation remains appropriately unresolved

I'm glad Claude didn't manufacture a B65 limit from neighboring products or reinterpret the unexplained `temp2_max=60°C`.

The useful facts remain device-reported protection points and Linux driver semantics. The soak establishes observed behavior below those protection points. Neither establishes Intel's unpublished recommended continuous operating temperature.

So **“maximum safe B65 temperature” remains unknown**, and it doesn't prevent us from establishing our own conservative operational policy from measured behavior.

### There are also two secondary findings worth preserving

The busiest CPU core reaching **98% while total CPU was only 28%** supports the existing observation that a single-thread bottleneck remains somewhere in the llama.cpp path. That's now worth keeping on the future optimization list, but not disturbing the current system over.

And the workload design was better than simply “54 minutes at full load”: approximately 22 minutes decode-heavy followed by 22 minutes of unique ~14K-token prompts exercised two materially different inference regimes. That helps explain why we saw very different KV/cache and prompt/decode behavior while watching the TUI.

Your auditory observation belongs in the evidence package too, but exactly as we just scoped it: **no conspicuous fan-noise excursion was perceived by the operator in a noisy multi-host environment**. It shouldn't be used to infer RPM or cooling-controller behavior.

Overall, I would accept this soak as **strong evidence for thermal adequacy within the tested operating envelope**, subject to reproducing Claude's calculations from the preserved raw evidence before treating the numerical conclusions as independently corroborated.

And I would leave every threshold unchanged for the moment.

The experiment has done something better than giving us an arbitrary new set of numbers. It has given us enough evidence to now design the **temperature policy deliberately**: separate package from VRAM, separate warning from protective action, decide whether persistence/hysteresis belongs in each, and determine the operational margins we actually want.

That should be a small follow-on analysis, not another blind soak.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Second, deliberately different implementation used to cross-check the published soak numbers.

Differences from analyze.py on purpose: generic recursive data walking (no hard-coded record layout), regex counting
of throttle flags straight from the raw text, Theil-Sen slopes on 10 s decimated points, rise time = first sustained
(5 consecutive samples) crossing of the *unsmoothed* signal, a different single-sample-spike definition (+-2 neighbours),
phase membership taken from each sample's own phase label, and request time assigned by completion time.
It does NOT reuse any code from analyze.py. Same author, so this is a second implementation, not third-party review."""
import hashlib, json, math, os, re, statistics as st, sys
RAW = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "..", "raw", "thermal-soak-20261003T170044Z")
SUM = json.load(open(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "summary.json")))
results = []
def check(name, published, recomputed, tol, unit=""):
    ok = abs(published - recomputed) <= tol
    results.append(ok); print(f"  [{'OK  ' if ok else 'DIFF'}] {name:58s} published {published:>9.2f}  recomputed {recomputed:>9.2f}  (tol {tol}{unit})")
def exact(name, published, recomputed):
    ok = published == recomputed; results.append(ok); print(f"  [{'OK  ' if ok else 'DIFF'}] {name:58s} published {published!s:>9}  recomputed {recomputed!s:>9}")
print("0. INTEGRITY: raw files against the hashes taken on the host")
host = dict(l.split()[::-1] for l in open(os.path.join(RAW, "..", "host-sha256.txt")).read().splitlines())
bad = [f for f, h in host.items() if hashlib.sha256(open(os.path.join(RAW, f), "rb").read()).hexdigest() != h]
exact("files whose hash differs from the host copy", 0, len(bad))
raw_lines = open(os.path.join(RAW, "samples.jsonl")).read().splitlines(); rows = [json.loads(l) for l in raw_lines]
def walk(o, path=()):
    if isinstance(o, dict):
        for k, v in o.items(): yield from walk(v, path + (k,))
    else: yield path, o
def per_gpu(row, key):          # all (gpu, subpath, value) whose path contains `key`
    return [(p[1], p[p.index(key) + 1:], v) for p, v in walk(row["gpu"], ("gpu",)) if key in p]
gpus = sorted(rows[0]["gpu"]); t = [r["t"] for r in rows]; phase = [r["phase"] for r in rows]
loaded = [i for i, p in enumerate(phase) if p in ("decode", "prefill")]
print("\n1. RUN SHAPE")
exact("samples", 3244, len(rows)); exact("loaded samples (decode+prefill, by each sample's own label)", 2640, len(loaded))
print("\n2. THROTTLE FLAGS, counted by regex on the raw text (independent of record layout)")
thermalish = sum(len(re.findall(r'"(?:thermal|prochot|vr_thermalert|ratl)": "(?!0")[^"]*"', l)) for l in raw_lines)
exact("non-zero thermal/prochot/vr_thermalert/ratl flags in whole run", 0, thermalish)
pl2_by_gpu = {g: 0 for g in gpus}; loaded_pl2 = {g: 0 for g in gpus}
for i, r in enumerate(rows):
    for g, sub, v in per_gpu(r, "flags"):
        if sub[0] if False else (sub and sub[-1] == "pl2") and v not in (None, "0"):
            pl2_by_gpu[g] += 1; loaded_pl2[g] += i in set(loaded)
exact("GPU0 PL2 samples (any phase)", 0, pl2_by_gpu[gpus[0]]); exact("GPU1 PL2 samples (any phase)", SUM["flags_whole_run"].get("gpu1.gt0.pl2", 0), pl2_by_gpu[gpus[1]])
check("GPU1 PL2 share of loaded samples (%)", 94.0, 100 * loaded_pl2[gpus[1]] / len(loaded), 0.2, " pp")
print("\n3. PLATEAUS AND SLOPES (last 300 s of each load phase)")
def series(g, name): return [r["gpu"][g]["temps"][name] for r in rows]
def window(p, a, b): return [i for i in range(len(rows)) if phase[i] == p and a <= t[i] < b]
def theil_sen(xs, ys):
    pts = list(zip(xs[::10], ys[::10])); sl = [(y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) for k, (x1, y1) in enumerate(pts) for (x2, y2) in pts[k + 1:] if x2 > x1]
    return 60 * st.median(sl)
wins = {"decode": (1140, 1440), "prefill": (2461, 2761)}; worst_slope = 0
for gi, g in enumerate(gpus):
    for name, key in (("pkg", "pkg"), ("vram", "vram")):
        y = series(g, key)
        for p, (a, b) in wins.items():
            idx = window(p, a, b); yy = [y[i] for i in idx]; pub = SUM["temps"][f"gpu{gi}"][name][p]
            check(f"gpu{gi} {name} {p} steady-state mean (C)", pub["mean"], st.mean(yy), 0.15)
            exact(f"gpu{gi} {name} {p} steady-state min / max", f'{pub["min"]:.0f}/{pub["max"]:.0f}', f"{min(yy):.0f}/{max(yy):.0f}")
